world.title: Russian strikes deepen Ukraine’s winter and budget crisis
world.summary: Ukraine is preparing for a severe winter as intensified Russian attacks damage energy infrastructure, export industries and other economic assets, Ukrainian officials said on Sept. 12. Economy Minister Oleksandr Kravchenko estimated damage to infrastructure and fixed assets this year at about $10 billion. He said the b
world.content: Ukraine is preparing for a severe winter as intensified Russian attacks damage energy infrastructure, export industries and other economic assets, Ukrainian officials said on Sept. 12. Economy Minister Oleksandr Kravchenko estimated damage to infrastructure and fixed assets this year at about $10 billion. He said the broader economic cost of the attacks and the effective blockade of Black Sea ports could reduce gross domestic product by about 1.5 percentage points. Russian strikes across Ukraine killed at least eight civilians and wounded dozens, according to local officials cited by The Associated Press. Residential areas in Zaporizhzhia, Kryvyi Rih, Odesa and Kramatorsk were hit, while an Odesa high-rise sustained extensive damage. Russian President Vladimir Putin separately warned from the BRICS summit in New Delhi that deploying European troops in Ukraine would mean “a war with Russia,” while saying Moscow did not threaten European countries.

world.title: Danish postwar drama wins Venice Golden Lion
world.summary: May el-Toukhy’s Danish-Egyptian postwar drama “Woman Unknown” won the Golden Lion for best film at the 83rd Venice Film Festival on Saturday, September 12. Mathilde Arcel, who plays a housemaid hiding a wartime relationship with a German soldier, won the Volpi Cup for best actress, giving the film both the Golden Lion
world.content: May el-Toukhy’s Danish-Egyptian postwar drama “Woman Unknown” won the Golden Lion for best film at the 83rd Venice Film Festival on Saturday, September 12. Mathilde Arcel, who plays a housemaid hiding a wartime relationship with a German soldier, won the Volpi Cup for best actress, giving the film both the Golden Lion and an acting prize. The film is set in Denmark after liberation from Nazi occupation, when women accused of relationships with German soldiers faced public persecution. Lee Chang-dong’s “Possible Love” won the Grand Jury Prize, Ilya Khrzhanovsky received the directing award for “DAU,” and John Malkovich won best actor for “Wild Horse Nine”. The Israeli-directed Gaza documentary “NAZA,” by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, received the Special Jury Prize after its premiere drew a 25-minute standing ovation.
world.image_alt: Danish postwar drama wins Venice Golden Lion

world.title: Saudi Arabia shuts oil pipeline after drone attack launched from Iraq
world.summary: Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its 1,200-kilometre East-West oil pipeline after several drones struck facilities in the Riyadh and Medina regions, causing injuries and damage, according to Saudi authorities. The pipeline links Abqaiq in the east to Yanbu on the Red Sea and had become a crucial alternative export route a
world.content: Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its 1,200-kilometre East-West oil pipeline after several drones struck facilities in the Riyadh and Medina regions, causing injuries and damage, according to Saudi authorities. The pipeline links Abqaiq in the east to Yanbu on the Red Sea and had become a crucial alternative export route after the Strait of Hormuz was largely blocked amid the war. The line had carried about 4 million to 5 million barrels of crude per day in recent months, equivalent to roughly 4% to 5% of global oil supply. Saudi Arabia and Iraq said the drones originated in Iraq, where Iran-backed militias operate. Iraq ordered an investigation, while Saudi Arabia said it would not retaliate immediately, following a request from Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi.
world.image_alt: Saudi Arabia shuts oil pipeline after drone attack launched from Iraq

world.title: Germany sees mass protests after AfD state election win
world.summary: About 150,000 people demonstrated in roughly 20 German cities on Saturday, September 12, against the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), according to organisers. The protests followed the AfD’s victory in Saxony-Anhalt’s September 6 state election, where it won nearly 44% of the vote and sought partners to form Ge
world.content: About 150,000 people demonstrated in roughly 20 German cities on Saturday, September 12, against the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), according to organisers. The protests followed the AfD’s victory in Saxony-Anhalt’s September 6 state election, where it won nearly 44% of the vote and sought partners to form Germany’s first far-right state government since World War II. Demonstrators in Berlin, Hamburg and Munich carried signs calling for the party to be banned and for democracy to be defended. The protests included an AfD counter-demonstration in Berlin. Chancellor Friedrich Merz and his centre-right CDU remain sceptical of pursuing a party ban. Under German law, only the Bundestag, Bundesrat or federal government may apply to the Federal Constitutional Court for a ban.
world.image_alt: Germany sees mass protests after AfD state election win

world.title: Reform UK receives record £72m from crypto billionaires
world.summary: Reform UK, the anti-immigration party led by Nigel Farage, has received two £36 million donations from cryptocurrency billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne about 24 hours apart. The combined £72 million is tied for the largest donation ever made to a British political party and exceeds the total donations rece
world.content: Reform UK, the anti-immigration party led by Nigel Farage, has received two £36 million donations from cryptocurrency billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne about 24 hours apart. The combined £72 million is tied for the largest donation ever made to a British political party and exceeds the total donations received by all UK parties in the previous year. Delo said he wanted to give Reform a “fair fight” against better-funded parties, while Harborne described his contribution as a philanthropic gift intended to help the party prepare for government. Police are investigating allegations that Reform accepted illegal foreign donations, which the party denies. Parliament’s standards watchdog is examining a separate £5 million personal gift Harborne gave Farage that was not declared in the lawmaker’s register of interests. Reform says it will use the new funding to strengthen its organisation ahead of the next general election, due by 2029. Established parties have called for tighter controls on political donations.
world.image_alt: Reform UK receives record £72m from crypto billionaires

world.title: Philippine ferry fire death toll reaches 76
world.summary: The death toll from the fire aboard the M/V June Aster rose to 76 after rescuers recovered 41 additional bodies from the burned-out vessel off Coron, Palawan, Philippine authorities said Saturday. Thirteen people remain unaccounted for, while 43 survivors have been recorded. The ferry left Manila carrying more than 130
world.content: The death toll from the fire aboard the M/V June Aster rose to 76 after rescuers recovered 41 additional bodies from the burned-out vessel off Coron, Palawan, Philippine authorities said Saturday. Thirteen people remain unaccounted for, while 43 survivors have been recorded. The ferry left Manila carrying more than 130 people and caught fire Wednesday evening near the end of its voyage to Coron, about 2.2 kilometers offshore. Search teams could not enter parts of the vessel until Friday because of toxic fumes and extreme heat. Authorities found many of the remains in the economy accommodation section and transported them to Coron, where forensic teams are using personal belongings and DNA samples to identify victims. Investigators are reviewing survivor accounts describing explosions before the blaze, a possible fire in the cargo hold and a rapid spread through passenger areas; the cause has not been established.
world.image_alt: Philippine ferry fire death toll reaches 76

world.title: Sweden votes as far right seeks cabinet posts
world.summary: Swedes voted Sunday in a closely contested parliamentary election pitting Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s center-right alliance against a center-left bloc led by former Prime Minister Magdalena Andersson. Kristersson has pledged cabinet posts to the Sweden Democrats if his bloc remains in power, putting the anti-immig
world.content: Swedes voted Sunday in a closely contested parliamentary election pitting Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s center-right alliance against a center-left bloc led by former Prime Minister Magdalena Andersson. Kristersson has pledged cabinet posts to the Sweden Democrats if his bloc remains in power, putting the anti-immigration party in government for the first time; Andersson is seeking to return to the premiership after four years in opposition. The Sweden Democrats have backed Kristersson’s minority government in parliament since 2022 but have not held ministerial posts. The campaign focused on immigration, organized crime, security, welfare spending and household costs. The right credited its policies with reducing gang violence and asylum applications, while the opposition said purchasing power and economic performance had deteriorated. More than 8 million people were eligible to vote for all 349 seats in the Riksdag, with polling stations open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. local time.
world.image_alt: Sweden votes as far right seeks cabinet posts

world.title: Houthis claim missile and drone attack on Saudi base
world.summary: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi movement said Sunday that it used missiles and drones against the Sharurah military base in southern Saudi Arabia, targeting weapons depots and command-and-control centers. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree did not specify when the operation occurred, and Saudi authorities did not immedi
world.content: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi movement said Sunday that it used missiles and drones against the Sharurah military base in southern Saudi Arabia, targeting weapons depots and command-and-control centers. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree did not specify when the operation occurred, and Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm whether the base was damaged. The claim followed a week of intensified fighting along Yemen’s Red Sea coast between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized government. Government forces said they struck Houthi positions near the port city of Mocha and in the Mocha-Dhubab area, while Saudi Civil Defence reported that a separate projectile hit Jazan province, wounding two people and damaging a mosque, buildings and vehicles.
world.image_alt: Houthis claim missile and drone attack on Saudi base

business.title: SEBI proposes two methods for derivatives expiry pricing
business.summary: India’s Securities and Exchange Board of India has proposed two alternatives for calculating settlement prices on expiry days for index and stock derivatives after concerns over price swings linked to the recently introduced Closing Auction Session (CAS). One option would combine volume-weighted average prices with the
business.content: India’s Securities and Exchange Board of India has proposed two alternatives for calculating settlement prices on expiry days for index and stock derivatives after concerns over price swings linked to the recently introduced Closing Auction Session (CAS). One option would combine volume-weighted average prices with the CAS price, while the other would retain the current methodology for at least a year. SEBI is also consulting on changes to the timing of continuous trading, the CAS and derivatives trading, including a transition break and longer intervals for some sessions. The proposals also cover order cancellations and Iceberg orders during the auction. Stakeholders have until October 3 to submit feedback.
business.image_alt: SEBI proposes two methods for derivatives expiry pricing

business.title: South Korea expands espionage law to protect chip secrets
business.summary: South Korea’s expanded espionage law took effect on Sept. 13, extending espionage offences beyond conduct benefiting North Korea to acts carried out for any foreign country or equivalent organisation. The amendment creates a new offence carrying a minimum prison sentence of three years, while existing provisions coveri
business.content: South Korea’s expanded espionage law took effect on Sept. 13, extending espionage offences beyond conduct benefiting North Korea to acts carried out for any foreign country or equivalent organisation. The amendment creates a new offence carrying a minimum prison sentence of three years, while existing provisions covering espionage for an “enemy state” remain in force. The National Assembly approved the revised Criminal Act on Feb. 26 after years of criticism that prosecutors had limited tools in cases involving foreign governments or companies. Seoul says the change will help protect semiconductors, displays, batteries, artificial intelligence and other strategic technologies. The law was promulgated on March 12 and followed a six-month grace period.
business.image_alt: South Korea expands espionage law to protect chip secrets

business.title: U.S. inflation outpaces wages as diesel prices surge
business.summary: U.S. consumer prices rose 3.4% in August from a year earlier, while average hourly pay increased 3.1%, leaving real hourly earnings down 0.3% from August 2025 and 0.1% from July, according to figures cited by CNBC. The decline reduced households' purchasing power after wages generally grew faster than inflation from Ma
business.content: U.S. consumer prices rose 3.4% in August from a year earlier, while average hourly pay increased 3.1%, leaving real hourly earnings down 0.3% from August 2025 and 0.1% from July, according to figures cited by CNBC. The decline reduced households' purchasing power after wages generally grew faster than inflation from May 2023 through spring 2026. Energy costs drove much of the latest pressure. Gasoline prices rose 3.9% in August, while diesel prices reached as high as $9.99 at a California station, according to reports cited by CNBC and AP. U.S. home sales weakened in August, while renewed fighting in the Middle East contributed to higher fuel prices.

business.title: BRICS adopts New Delhi declaration amid Middle East war
business.summary: BRICS leaders unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration at their summit in New Delhi on September 12, calling for maximum restraint in the Middle East, peaceful dispute resolution, and protection of civilian infrastructure and safeguarded nuclear facilities. The statement also condemned unilateral sanctions and rai
business.content: BRICS leaders unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration at their summit in New Delhi on September 12, calling for maximum restraint in the Middle East, peaceful dispute resolution, and protection of civilian infrastructure and safeguarded nuclear facilities. The statement also condemned unilateral sanctions and raised concerns about unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures that distort trade, while committing members to support global trade, supply chains and energy flows. India used its 2026 chairmanship to press for greater Global South representation in the UN Security Council and international financial institutions, alongside a 10-point roadmap for more representative global governance. The declaration followed a failed BRICS foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi in May and negotiations over differences involving Iran and the United Arab Emirates. China’s President Xi Jinping said Beijing would work with BRICS members for peace in West Asia.
business.image_alt: BRICS adopts New Delhi declaration amid Middle East war

business.title: Canada seeks $1tn as Carney pitches investment summit
business.summary: Canada is seeking as much as $1tn from investors as Prime Minister Mark Carney prepares to host an investment summit in Toronto aimed at attracting capital and supporting his plan to reduce the economy’s dependence on the United States. The summit is scheduled for next week and will bring together senior executives fro
business.content: Canada is seeking as much as $1tn from investors as Prime Minister Mark Carney prepares to host an investment summit in Toronto aimed at attracting capital and supporting his plan to reduce the economy’s dependence on the United States. The summit is scheduled for next week and will bring together senior executives from global financial firms. Carney is presenting Canada as a destination for investors seeking alternatives to the United States under President Donald Trump. The government’s pitch links the fundraising target to a broader capital agenda focused on attracting foreign money and strengthening Canada’s economic position.

business.title: President Trump threatens Canada trade pact as talks stall
business.summary: Canada is the largest foreign buyer of U.S. goods, the second-largest export market for American farmers after Mexico, and receives most U.S. products duty-free under the North American trade pact. The countries remain involved in a tariff dispute. President Trump said on Sept. 12 that a new trade deal with Canada coul
business.content: Canada is the largest foreign buyer of U.S. goods, the second-largest export market for American farmers after Mexico, and receives most U.S. products duty-free under the North American trade pact. The countries remain involved in a tariff dispute. President Trump said on Sept. 12 that a new trade deal with Canada could come “fairly soon,” though it was unclear whether formal negotiations had begun. The dispute has also prompted debate in Canada over reliance on U.S. technology and the difficulty of developing alternatives while retaining the ability to regulate digital issues.

business.title: Saudi Arabia shuts oil pipeline after Iraqi drone attacks
business.summary: Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its 1,200-kilometre East-West oil pipeline after drones struck facilities in the Riyadh and Medina regions on Thursday, causing injuries and damage, Saudi authorities said. The pipeline links Abqaiq near the Gulf to Yanbu on the Red Sea and had become a key export route after war-related d
business.content: Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its 1,200-kilometre East-West oil pipeline after drones struck facilities in the Riyadh and Medina regions on Thursday, causing injuries and damage, Saudi authorities said. The pipeline links Abqaiq near the Gulf to Yanbu on the Red Sea and had become a key export route after war-related disruption sharply reduced tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia said the drones came from Iraq, while Baghdad confirmed the attack originated in its territory and ordered an investigation. Iraq also dismissed the military commander responsible for operations in Maysan province, near Iran. Riyadh said it would not retaliate following a request from Iraq’s prime minister but reserved the right to take measures to protect its territory and facilities. President Trump said Iran was probably responsible for the attack without providing evidence.
business.image_alt: Saudi Arabia shuts oil pipeline after Iraqi drone attacks

business.title: ECB’s Lagarde warns inflation shock will last longer
business.summary: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said the euro area’s inflation shock will last longer than expected after the ECB raised interest rates for a second time since the Iran war drove oil and natural-gas prices higher. Euro-area inflation remains above 3%, and the ECB raised its inflation projections for 2
business.content: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said the euro area’s inflation shock will last longer than expected after the ECB raised interest rates for a second time since the Iran war drove oil and natural-gas prices higher. Euro-area inflation remains above 3%, and the ECB raised its inflation projections for 2027 and 2028; it expects inflation in 2028 to remain slightly above the bank’s 2% target. The ECB lifted its deposit rate to 2.5%. Lagarde said prolonged energy-market volatility could keep inflation elevated as the conflict in the Middle East continues. She said higher energy costs could weigh on growth, although the euro-area economy has so far shown resilience to the conflict and U.S. trade policies; the ECB also raised its growth forecasts. Mortgage rates have risen in several major euro-area economies, with quoted fixed rates ranging from about 2.2% in Spain to an average of 4.46% in Germany, though loan terms differ.
business.image_alt: ECB’s Lagarde warns inflation shock will last longer

science.title: Rubin Observatory images famous COSMOS deep field
science.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has turned its survey capabilities toward the COSMOS field, a well-studied region of the universe in the constellation Sextans. The Hubble Space Telescope photographed the field in segments from 2003 to 2005. Astronomers combined those images with observations from ground-based and other s
science.content: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has turned its survey capabilities toward the COSMOS field, a well-studied region of the universe in the constellation Sextans. The Hubble Space Telescope photographed the field in segments from 2003 to 2005. Astronomers combined those images with observations from ground-based and other space telescopes to show large-scale patterns of cosmic evolution. Rubin is designed for rapid, wide-field imaging of the sky.
science.image_alt: Rubin Observatory images famous COSMOS deep field

science.title: AI leaders urge slower development after extinction warnings
science.summary: A former Anthropic researcher warned that rapidly advancing artificial intelligence could threaten humanity, prompting public responses from leaders of competing AI companies. Jacob Coxon said people building advanced systems were “genuinely frightened” by the pace of progress and warned that failing to slow developmen
science.content: A former Anthropic researcher warned that rapidly advancing artificial intelligence could threaten humanity, prompting public responses from leaders of competing AI companies. Jacob Coxon said people building advanced systems were “genuinely frightened” by the pace of progress and warned that failing to slow development could lead to mass death. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing capability gains so safety work can catch up. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and xAI founder Elon Musk supported Amodei’s call for slower development and independent monitoring. Amodei warned that a more capable swarm of AI agents could control internet-connected computers within six to 12 months. Researchers and commentators disagree about the immediacy and probability of an extinction scenario. Stuart Russell said current systems do not pose the superintelligence risks under discussion and identified malicious human use as the nearer-term danger. Other analysts argued that takeover scenarios do not require literal human extinction.
science.image_alt: AI leaders urge slower development after extinction warnings

science.title: Study suggests young Sun swallowed a super-Earth
science.summary: A study proposes that the young Sun may have consumed a rocky super-Earth several times more massive than Earth. Published in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, the research suggests the collision could help explain the Sun’s unusually low lithium abundance and other unexplained features.
science.content: A study proposes that the young Sun may have consumed a rocky super-Earth several times more massive than Earth. Published in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, the research suggests the collision could help explain the Sun’s unusually low lithium abundance and other unexplained features.
science.image_alt: Study suggests young Sun swallowed a super-Earth

science.title: OpenAI claims AI agents found Navier-Stokes result
science.summary: OpenAI has claimed that a system using roughly 10,000 AI agents found a result related to the Navier-Stokes equations, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems. The company said the agents worked in parallel for 88 hours; estimates put the effort's cost at about $15 million. The Clay Mathematics Institute offers a $1
science.content: OpenAI has claimed that a system using roughly 10,000 AI agents found a result related to the Navier-Stokes equations, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems. The company said the agents worked in parallel for 88 hours; estimates put the effort's cost at about $15 million. The Clay Mathematics Institute offers a $1 million prize for a valid solution. The claim has prompted scrutiny because the reported result appears to identify a situation in which the equations break down, rather than provide the general proof mathematicians have sought for decades. Researchers have also questioned attribution and whether OpenAI drew on ideas developed by NYU mathematicians Tristan Buckmaster and Levent Alpöge. Buckmaster said OpenAI eventually acknowledged that it sent its first prompt after information about their work had reached the company. OpenAI's announcement initially did not mention the researchers, according to reporting from La Voz de Galicia.
science.image_alt: OpenAI claims AI agents found Navier-Stokes result

science.title: Anthropic blocks Claude use linked to biological weapons research
science.summary: Anthropic said it blocked efforts to use its Claude artificial-intelligence models for activity that could have supported biological weapons, including research involving the Chikungunya virus. The company said it suspended accounts and strengthened safeguards. Anthropic’s September 2026 threat-intelligence report exam
science.content: Anthropic said it blocked efforts to use its Claude artificial-intelligence models for activity that could have supported biological weapons, including research involving the Chikungunya virus. The company said it suspended accounts and strengthened safeguards. Anthropic’s September 2026 threat-intelligence report examined potential abuse between December 2025 and August 2026. The company said the cases involved dual-use biological research but did not claim the researchers intended to develop biological weapons.
science.image_alt: Anthropic blocks Claude use linked to biological weapons research

science.title: Japanese island leopard cats show unexplained short-tail trait
science.summary: Scientists identified an unusual short-tail trait in three Tsushima leopard cats observed on Japan’s Tsushima Island in 2024 and 2025. The cats’ tails measured about half the usual average length, and researchers said the feature had not previously been reported in this population or any other leopard-cat population. A
science.content: Scientists identified an unusual short-tail trait in three Tsushima leopard cats observed on Japan’s Tsushima Island in 2024 and 2025. The cats’ tails measured about half the usual average length, and researchers said the feature had not previously been reported in this population or any other leopard-cat population. About 100 Tsushima leopard cats remain on the island, where the population is considered critically endangered. Because short tails are common among domestic cats on Tsushima, researchers examined whether the trait could result from hybridization. They sequenced the whole genome of one short-tailed leopard cat; Nikkei reported that Anicom’s analysis found the trait was not derived from domestic cats. The researchers said the repeated occurrence makes separate traumatic injuries less likely and raises the possibility of a shared hereditary or developmental cause.
science.image_alt: Japanese island leopard cats show unexplained short-tail trait

science.title: RHS advises English gardeners to drop cauliflower crops
science.summary: The Royal Horticultural Society is advising gardeners in England to stop growing cauliflower because high temperatures are preventing the crop from producing good heads. The warning also covers related brassicas, including broccoli and cabbage. Farmers expect a poor harvest and say drought could make this one of the wo
science.content: The Royal Horticultural Society is advising gardeners in England to stop growing cauliflower because high temperatures are preventing the crop from producing good heads. The warning also covers related brassicas, including broccoli and cabbage. Farmers expect a poor harvest and say drought could make this one of the worst years on record.
science.image_alt: RHS advises English gardeners to drop cauliflower crops

science.title: Study warns Atlantic current collapse could disrupt food production
science.summary: An international research team examined the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, or AMOC, as human-caused climate change weakens it. Its decline could alter the temperature and rainfall patterns used to grow food.
science.content: An international research team examined the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, or AMOC, as human-caused climate change weakens it. Its decline could alter the temperature and rainfall patterns used to grow food.

sports.title: No. 4 Texas rallies past No. 1 Ohio State 24-23
sports.summary: No. 4 Texas defeated No. 1 Ohio State 24-23 in Austin on Sept. 12 after erasing a 20-point fourth-quarter deficit. The Longhorns trailed 23-3 after three quarters before scoring 21 unanswered points and completing the comeback on Hollywood Smothers’ 1-yard touchdown run with 25 seconds remaining. Arch Manning started t
sports.content: No. 4 Texas defeated No. 1 Ohio State 24-23 in Austin on Sept. 12 after erasing a 20-point fourth-quarter deficit. The Longhorns trailed 23-3 after three quarters before scoring 21 unanswered points and completing the comeback on Hollywood Smothers’ 1-yard touchdown run with 25 seconds remaining. Arch Manning started the rally with a touchdown pass to Ryan Wingo and used his legs to sustain later drives. After Smothers’ earlier touchdown brought Texas within one score, Ohio State had a chance to extend its lead, but Connor Hawkins missed a 45-yard field goal. Texas then drove for the winning touchdown. The result gave Texas a 2-0 record and left Ohio State 1-1.
sports.image_alt: No. 4 Texas rallies past No. 1 Ohio State 24-23

sports.title: U.S., Europe tied 8-8 before Solheim Cup singles
sports.summary: The United States rallied to draw level with Europe at 8-8 after the second day of the Solheim Cup at Bernardus Golf in Den Bosch, Netherlands, setting up 12 singles matches on Sunday, September 13. Europe won Saturday morning’s foursomes 3-1 to lead 7-5, but the United States won the afternoon fourballs by the same ma
sports.content: The United States rallied to draw level with Europe at 8-8 after the second day of the Solheim Cup at Bernardus Golf in Den Bosch, Netherlands, setting up 12 singles matches on Sunday, September 13. Europe won Saturday morning’s foursomes 3-1 to lead 7-5, but the United States won the afternoon fourballs by the same margin. Jennifer Kupcho and Lindy Duncan secured the final American point by beating Carlota Ciganda and Celine Boutier 1-up. Maja Stark and Linn Grant defeated Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz 3&2 in the morning before beating Megan Khang and Lauren Coughlin 2&1 in the afternoon. Charley Hull and Solheim Cup debutant Lottie Woad lost both of their Saturday matches, leaving them with half a point from four outings. Europe needs 6.5 points from the singles to win the trophy outright, while the United States needs six points to retain it.
sports.image_alt: U.S., Europe tied 8-8 before Solheim Cup singles

sports.title: Ipswich beat 10-man Crystal Palace 3-2 on late goal
sports.summary: Ipswich Town beat Crystal Palace 3-2 at Selhurst Park on Saturday, September 12, after Zian Flemming scored his first goal for the club in the 90th minute. Palace opened the scoring through Anan Khalaili, but Ipswich responded with goals from Emersonn and Leif Davis before half-time. Jørgen Strand Larsen equalised for
sports.content: Ipswich Town beat Crystal Palace 3-2 at Selhurst Park on Saturday, September 12, after Zian Flemming scored his first goal for the club in the 90th minute. Palace opened the scoring through Anan Khalaili, but Ipswich responded with goals from Emersonn and Leif Davis before half-time. Jørgen Strand Larsen equalised for Palace in the 75th minute, but Flemming settled the match late. Crystal Palace were reduced to 10 men in the 34th minute when Axel Disasi received a straight red card for a high-footed challenge on Jack Clarke. Ipswich ended a two-match losing run and claimed their second Premier League win of the season, while Palace suffered their third defeat in four league matches.
sports.image_alt: Ipswich beat 10-man Crystal Palace 3-2 on late goal

sports.title: Springboks win Baltimore finale against All Blacks
sports.summary: South Africa defeated New Zealand 43-28 in Baltimore on September 12 to win the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series 3-1. The Springboks led 17-14 at halftime before outscoring New Zealand 26-14 in the second half, scoring six tries to the All Blacks’ four. Kurt-Lee Arendse’s long solo try, after the All Blacks cu
sports.content: South Africa defeated New Zealand 43-28 in Baltimore on September 12 to win the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series 3-1. The Springboks led 17-14 at halftime before outscoring New Zealand 26-14 in the second half, scoring six tries to the All Blacks’ four. Kurt-Lee Arendse’s long solo try, after the All Blacks cut the deficit to 29-21, extended South Africa’s lead. Cameron Hanekom added a late score before Beauden Barrett replied in the final minute. The match at M&T Bank Stadium drew 68,173 spectators, the largest crowd for a rugby match in the United States. The result completed a series in which New Zealand won the opener before South Africa claimed the next three Tests. South Africa’s advantage came at the breakdown, set piece and in aerial contests. A first-half communications failure among match officials caused a stoppage of more than eight minutes.
sports.image_alt: Springboks win Baltimore finale against All Blacks

sports.title: Liverpool held by Fulham as Anfield winless run extends
sports.summary: Liverpool drew 0-0 with Fulham at Anfield on September 12, earning Fulham their first Premier League point of the season and extending Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola’s unbeaten start to four league matches. Liverpool struggled to create clear chances despite starting Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak,
sports.content: Liverpool drew 0-0 with Fulham at Anfield on September 12, earning Fulham their first Premier League point of the season and extending Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola’s unbeaten start to four league matches. Liverpool struggled to create clear chances despite starting Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak, while Fulham posed the greater threat for long periods. Iraola said Liverpool lacked freshness after beating Atlético Madrid 2-1 in the Champions League less than 72 hours earlier and identified a lack of attacking output as the decisive problem. Liverpool remain without a home league win this season, while Fulham ended a run of three consecutive defeats under former Liverpool defender Álvaro Arbeloa.
sports.image_alt: Liverpool held by Fulham as Anfield winless run extends

sports.title: Manchester derby tests Maresca’s City and Carrick’s United

sports.content: Manchester United host Manchester City at Old Trafford on Sunday, September 13, in the first Premier League Manchester derby of the 2026-27 season. City are top of the table with nine points from three matches and four consecutive wins in all competitions, while United have four points from three league games but beat Sabah 4-0 in the Champions League in midweek. The match is Enzo Maresca’s first derby as City manager and the 199th competitive meeting between the clubs. United have won nine of their 10 Premier League matches at Old Trafford in 2026, including a 2-0 victory over City in January. United drew 2-2 with Everton, while City won 2-0 at Porto in the Champions League, leaving both teams with a short turnaround from midweek European fixtures.

sports.content: Tottenham Hotspur drew 0-0 with Everton at home on September 12, extending their wait for a first Premier League win and goal under Roberto De Zerbi. Spurs have taken two points from four matches and sit 17th. They became the first Tottenham side to open a Premier League season without scoring in their first four games. Tottenham created little after a lively opening, while Everton produced the clearer second-half chances through Thierno Barry, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Brennan Johnson. De Zerbi attributed the slow start to injuries, late arrivals and limited preparation with the full squad. He also said the players must overcome a psychological blockage.

sports.content: England beat Pakistan by eight wickets in the third Test at Edgbaston on September 12 to complete a 3-0 series sweep. Chasing 130, England fell to 2-2 in the opening over after Mohammad Abbas dismissed Ben Duckett and Emilio Gay, but Joe Root made 62 not out and Jordan Cox 59 not out to complete the chase in 24.2 overs. It was England’s first home Test series whitewash against Pakistan. The sweep followed Ben Stokes’ retirement, Brendon McCullum’s departure from the Test coaching role and Root’s return as captain.
